title: Regular-sequence kernels along a surjection of regular local rings
statement: Let $u:U\twoheadrightarrow V$ and $v:V\twoheadrightarrow W$ be surjective local homomorphisms of commutative local rings (each has exactly one maximal ideal, and a local homomorphism carries the maximal ideal into the maximal ideal). Assume that $U$ and $V$ are regular local rings [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Then $\ker(v\circ u)$ is generated by a finite $U$-regular sequence contained in the maximal ideal of $U$ if and only if $\ker v$ is generated by a finite $V$-regular sequence contained in the maximal ideal of $V$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Empty generating sequences are allowed. No completeness assumption is made on these rings.

source.place: Tag 00SE, lemma-ci-well-defined (lines 36038–36053), equivalence of conditions (1) and (3).

proof.text: Put $I=\ker(vu)$ and $J=\ker u$. Surjectivity gives $J\subseteq I\subseteq\mathfrak m_U$ and $I/J\cong\ker v$; also $U/J\cong V$ and $U/I\cong W$. Put $d=\dim U$. The parameter theorems give $x_1,\ldots,x_d$ generating $\mathfrak m_U$, with $J=(x_1,\ldots,x_a)$ and $a=\dim U-\dim V\ge0$. The prefix quotients are regular local of dimension $d-c$, so $a=0$ gives $J=0$.

source.place: Tag 00SE, kernel setup and parameter count; Tags 00NR and 00NQ.

proof.text: For every regular local ring $R$ used below, a full parameter sequence is regular of length $\dim R$. The definition of depth gives $\operatorname{depth}R\ge\dim R$; the depth bound applied to the finite nonzero module $R$ gives the reverse inequality, since its support is all of $\operatorname{Spec}R$. Thus the fixed-tuple criterion applies: a list of $r$ elements in $\mathfrak m_R$ is regular exactly when its quotient has dimension $\dim R-r$.

source.place: Tag 00SE, first proof paragraph; fixed-tuple version Tag 02JN and depth bound Tag 00LK.

proof.text: If $\ker v=(y_1,\ldots,y_b)$ is regular, Step 2 gives $b=\dim V-\dim W$. Lift each $y_i$ to $\widetilde y_i\in\mathfrak m_U$: a unit cannot map to a nonunit. The list $x_1,\ldots,x_a,\widetilde y_1,\ldots,\widetilde y_b$ generates $I$, given $h\in I$, lift coefficients expressing $u(h)$ in the $y_i$; subtracting that combination of $\widetilde y_i$ leaves an element of $J$. Its length is $\dim U-\dim W$, so Step 2 makes this list regular. Empty prefixes or tails are allowed.

source.place: Tag 00SE, (4) implies (2): lift quotient generators and adjoin generators of J.

proof.text: Conversely induct on $a$, simultaneously for all the stated surjections. If $a=0$, $u$ is an isomorphism; multiplication and quotient maps identify the successive nonzerodivisor conditions. Suppose $a>0$ and $I=(z_1,\ldots,z_b)$ is regular. Step 2 gives $b=\dim U-\dim W$. Apply the residue-basis lemma to this tuple. Apply it also to the full parameter tuple: $[x_1]\ne0$ in $\mathfrak m_U/\mathfrak m_U^2$. Since $I\subseteq\mathfrak m_U$, $\mathfrak m_UI\subseteq\mathfrak m_U^2$, hence $x_1\in J\setminus\mathfrak m_UI$. The same lemma gives $b>0$ and an exactly $b$-element generating list $x_1,z'_2,\ldots,z'_b$ for $I$.

source.place: Tag 00SE, final paragraph: induction setup, nonzero parameter class, exact generator count and Nakayama.

proof.text: Here $d=\dim U\ge a>0$ and $1\le b=d-\dim W\le d$, since $W$ is nonzero local. Apply the parameter-cut lemma to this list and $u$, using $\dim(U/I)=\dim W=\dim U-b$. It gives $U'=U/(x_1)$ regular local, a regular generating tuple of length $b-1$ for the image $I'$, and local surjections $U'\twoheadrightarrow V\twoheadrightarrow W$ with dimension difference $a-1$. For $q:U\to U'$, the induced composite kills $q(h)$ exactly when $vu(h)=0$, i.e. $h\in I$; hence its kernel is $q(I)=I'$. The induction hypothesis gives a regular sequence generating $\ker v$. The case $b=1$ uses the empty quotient tuple; $b=0$ cannot enter this branch.

The proof follows Stacks 00SE (algebra.tex 36038ff), which I read in full. Steps 1–2 use 00NR and 00NQ for the parameters and the prefix dimension a = dim U − dim V. Depth ≥ dim comes from 00NQ and the depth definition, and depth ≤ dim from 00LK applied with Supp R = Spec R; these feed the fixed-tuple CM criterion lem-trf-cm-regular-sequence-generator-count (02JN). Step 3 (forward): lifts of the y_i are nonunits, the lifted list generates I by lifting coefficients, and its length is dim U − dim W, so it is regular. Steps 4–5 (converse, induction on a): A applied to the regular parameter tuple makes [x_1] nonzero in m/m², and mI ⊆ m² gives x_1 ∈ J \ mI. A then gives b ≥ 1 and a b-element generating list starting with x_1. B gives U' = U/(x_1) regular local of dimension d − 1, a regular (b−1)-tuple generating I', and u' local with dimension difference a − 1. The kernel of U'→W is q(I), checked by representatives. New node A (residue basis and prescribed generator) is true: 00LN(1) gives the conormal basis, I² ⊆ mI gives the κ-basis of I/mI, and Nakayama (00DV) on the finite ideal gives the generation claim. I tested a field and I = (t²) in k[[t]]. New node B (parameter cut) is true by 00NQ (c = 1) and 02JN on R'; I tested I = (s, t²) in k[[s,t]] and the b = 1 case. lean.statement: theorem regularLocalSurjectionKernelComparison (U : Type u) (V : Type v) (W : Type w) [CommRing U] [CommRing V] [CommRing W] [IsLocalRing W] [IsRegularLocalRing U] [IsRegularLocalRing V] (u : U →+* V) (v : V →+* W) [IsLocalHom u] [IsLocalHom v] (hu : Function.Surjective u) (hv : Function.Surjective v) : ((∃ xs : List U, RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular U xs ∧ Ideal.ofList xs = RingHom.ker (v.comp u) ∧ ∀ x ∈ xs, x ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal U) ↔ (∃ ys : List V, RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular V ys ∧ Ideal.ofList ys = RingHom.ker v ∧ ∀ y ∈ ys, y ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal V))
